categories.name: LLM Agent Security Research
categories.summary: Significant research activity focused on securing LLM agents against adversarial attacks. Studies examine prompt injection vulnerabilities in agentic environments, threat surfaces unique to autonomous AI systems, and game-theoretic approaches to defend against context poisoning. The consensus emerging is that agent security requires fundamentally different approaches than traditional LLM safety.

key_items.title: Automated Prompt-Injection Attacks in AgentDojo Evaluated
key_items.detail: Empirical study finds black-box optimization (TAP) more reliable than white-box (GCG) for indirect prompt injection against LLM agents. Task-universal prompts transfer across tasks but not from smaller OSS models to frontier models like GPT-5.

key_items.title: Comprehensive LLM Agent Threat Surface Analysis
key_items.detail: New framework identifies that agent risk shifts from unsafe text generation to control-flow and state manipulation, where untrusted inputs can steer tool use and persistent memory across long-horizon tasks.

key_items.title: Game-Theoretic Defense Against Context Poisoning
key_items.detail: Research addresses how adversarial fragments can gradually distort LLM reasoning trajectories in multi-turn interactions, proposing game-theoretic multi-agent control mechanisms.

categories.name: AI-Powered Offensive Security
categories.summary: Proof-of-concept demonstrations show AI systems capable of autonomous offensive operations. A self-replicating worm using local open-weight models can reason about networks and generate tailored attack steps without relying on commercial AI APIs, raising significant concerns about democratized AI-enabled attacks.

key_items.title: Self-Replicating AI Worm PoC Using Local LLMs
key_items.detail: Researchers demonstrate a worm that uses locally hosted open-weight LLMs for autonomous target-by-target planning, capable of self-replication across networks without calling commercial AI services.

categories.name: AI Security Tools & Vulnerabilities
categories.summary: Practical security concerns continue with MCP (Model Context Protocol) vulnerabilities discovered in Claude Code that enable token theft via MITM attacks. This highlights the expanding attack surface as AI coding assistants gain deeper system integration.

key_items.title: Claude Code MCP Token Theft via MITM
key_items.detail: Mitiga researchers disclose a vulnerability in Claude Code's MCP implementation that allows attackers to intercept and steal authentication tokens through man-in-the-middle attacks.

categories.name: Standards & Policy
categories.summary: NIST released mathematical proof supporting the transition to continuous monitoring and update paradigms for security frameworks. This signals a formal shift toward adaptive security models that may better align with the pace of AI-driven threats.

key_items.title: NIST Mathematical Proof for Continuous Monitoring
key_items.detail: NIST publishes formal mathematical justification for transitioning security frameworks from periodic assessment to continuous monitoring and update cycles.

categories.name: AI-Assisted Security Practices
categories.summary: SANS Institute and Anthropic collaborate on structured methodologies for AI-assisted vulnerability analysis. The six-step loop approach aims to reduce ambiguity in LLM-assisted code review by making evidence collection and hypothesis testing explicit.

key_items.title: SEC543 AI-Enabled Code Vulnerability Analysis Loop
key_items.detail: A structured six-step methodology for AI-assisted code review keeps LLM output tied to concrete code paths through explicit evidence collection, hypothesis testing, and fix verification stages.

categories.name: Learning Resources & Curated Lists
categories.summary: Community-maintained resources for security professionals continue to expand, with curated repositories covering Microsoft security skills and LLM applications in cybersecurity providing structured learning paths for practitioners.

key_items.title: Microsoft Security Skills Repository
key_items.detail: GitHub repository aggregating Microsoft security certification paths and skill-building resources for security professionals.

key_items.title: Awesome LLM4Cybersecurity Collection
key_items.detail: Curated list of resources covering LLM applications in cybersecurity including offensive, defensive, and research applications.

top_insights: LLM agent security is rapidly becoming a distinct subfield, with research emphasizing that autonomous agents face fundamentally different threat models than conversational LLMs—particularly around control-flow hijacking and state persistence.

The gap between open-weight and frontier model security is widening: prompt injection techniques that work on smaller OSS models don't reliably transfer to GPT-5 class systems, suggesting defensive improvements at the frontier.
Self-replicating AI malware running on local models represents a concerning democratization of sophisticated attack capabilities that doesn't depend on API access to commercial providers.
Industry is formalizing AI-assisted security workflows with structured methodologies (SANS/Anthropic) to prevent LLM hallucination and keep analysis grounded in evidence.
NIST's mathematical backing for continuous monitoring signals regulatory momentum toward adaptive security frameworks that may become mandatory for AI system deployments.
